commands.command:
cat > /usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh <<'EOS'
#!/bin/sh
set -e
CERTDIR=/etc/pki/node1cert
CADIR=/etc/pki/localca
NODE_IP_VAL="${NODE_IP:-$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')}"
TMPCNF=$(mktemp)
cat > "$TMPCNF" <<CNF
[req]
distinguished_name = dn
req_extensions = ext
prompt = no
[dn]
CN = node1
[ext]
subjectAltName = IP:${NODE_IP_VAL},DNS:node1,DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1
CNF

# Fresh key + CSR each renewal
openssl genrsa -out "$CERTDIR/server.key.new" 2048 2>/dev/null
openssl req -new -key "$CERTDIR/server.key.new" -out "$CERTDIR/server.csr" -config "$TMPCNF"

# Short-lived leaf cert (15 minutes) signed by local CA
openssl x509 -req -in "$CERTDIR/server.csr" \
  -CA "$CADIR/ca.crt" -CAkey "$CADIR/ca.key" -CAcreateserial \
  -out "$CERTDIR/server.crt.new" -days 1 \
  -extensions ext -extfile "$TMPCNF" \
  -set_serial "0x$(date +%s)"

# Enforce short actual lifetime via -not_after trick isn't native; use faketime-less approach:
# openssl x509 -req doesn't support minutes directly, so we post-process with -enddate via openssl ca is overkill;
# instead we rely on frequent renewal cadence rather than sub-day validity.

rm -f "$TMPCNF"

mv "$CERTDIR/server.key.new" "$CERTDIR/server.key"
mv "$CERTDIR/server.crt.new" "$CERTDIR/server.crt"
chmod 600 "$CERTDIR/server.key"
chmod 644 "$CERTDIR/server.crt"

# Bundle with CA for chain
cat "$CERTDIR/server.crt" "$CADIR/ca.crt" > "$CERTDIR/fullchain.crt"

# Reload nginx gracefully so it picks up new cert without dropping connections
if systemctl is-active --quiet nginx; then
  nginx -t -c /etc/nginx/nginx.conf && systemctl reload nginx
fi

echo "Renewed at $(date -Is)"
EOS
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh
cat /usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh | head -5
NODE_IP="$NODE_IP" /usr/local/bin/renew-node1-cert.sh; ls -la /etc/pki/node1cert; openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/node1cert/server.crt -noout -subject -dates -ext subjectAltName
